This appeal is filed by the appellant/State being aggrieved of the judgment dated 06.04.2015 passed by learned Special Judge (Atrocities), Panna in Special Case No.05/2014, whereby learned trial Curt has acquitted the accused Vishnu Kushwaha,
son of Gopal Kushwaha from the charges under Sections 450, 376(1) and 506(Part-II) of IPC,
Section 3/4 of POCSO Act and Section 3(2)(v) of SC/ST Act.
2.
Allegation is that victim, resident of Village Bhatharmegha had lodged a report that she was studying in 10th Class.
On 30.11.2013, she was alone at home.
Her mother had gone to her elder sister's house at Village Umarhat, whereas her brothers had gone to earn their livelihood.
At about 10:00 a.m., she was cleaning her courtyard, then Vishnu Kushwaha entered into her house, closed the door and had thrown her on floor.
Thereafter, she was undressed and her privacy was violated.

3. On 12.12.2013, her mother returned back from the house of her elder sister, then she narrated her s t o r y t o h e r m o t h e r . M o t h e r i n t u r n i n f o r m e d t h e N E U T R A L C I T A T I O N N O .

sentences.text: It is submitted that trial Court has arbitrarily and without any justification recorded a finding of acquittal which calls for interference.

It is submitted that if the judgment of acquittal is allowed to stand, then it will embolden members of other communities other than Scheduled Caste to suppress members of Scheduled Caste category in the name of physical exploitation.
4. After hearing Shri Ajay Tamrakar, learned Govt. Advocate, it has come on record and not disputed that Ex.P-8 is the X-ray film available on record.

As per the report of the Radiologist from District Hospital, Panna, i.e. Ex.P- 9, it was noted by the concerned Medical Officer/In-charge X-ray Department, District Hospital, Panna that age of the victim was between 17 to 18 years.
5. It has also come on ecord that FIR Ex.P-1 was lodged on 12.12.2013 after 12 days of the incident.

It has also come on record that since victim was a consenting adult, it is not a case of violation of privacy, but a case of consensual relationship which cannot be termed to be covered by any of the charged sections.
6.
Victim was examined before the trial Court as PW-1.
She admitted that she was subjected to medical examination at District Hospital, Panna and medical examination was conducted after taking her consent.
PW-1 also admitted that X-ray is taken.
In para 10 of her cross-examination this witness admitted that her residential accommodation and that of the accused Vishnu are enclosed proximity in the village.
She admitted that sisters of Vishnu were studying with her in the same school along with other girls.
She admitted that she was visiting sisters of Vishnu from a time prior to the incident.
She stated that she had studied from 1st Class to 8th Class in a school at Bhatharmegha and then she completed 9th and 10th Class studies from Samardadha School.
She admitted that in Ex.D-2 statements have been recorded which were not given by her.
She admitted that around her house, there are several houses of persons belonging to her caste.
She also admitted NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:9384 3 CRA-166-2016 that there are 200 - 250 houses at Village Bhatharmegha.
She admitted that when allegedly accused had thrown her on floor, she could not raise an alarm.
There are contradictions that if accused was pressing her mouth so to not to permit her to sought, then how he could have opened her clothing with both the hands as stated by her.
She admits that during the whole course of interaction, no injuries were sustained by her on any part of the body.
She admitted that marriage of accused was performed two and half years prior to the incident and he has a daughter also who was born two and half months prior to the incident.
She admitted that she had not narrated about the incident to any of her friends.
She admitted that she had not asked her brothers to call her mother.
She admitted that she had performed her daily duties like preparing meals for brothers, performing Pooja, etc. every day.
She admitted that during the intercourse there was no bleeding.
She stated that she does not know as to who had admitted her in the school.
7. P.W.-2, mother of the victim, stated that she was visiting her elder daughter at her village.
She had left the victim and two of her sons at home and she returned back, then she was informed about the incident.
In cross- examination, this witness admitted that her son is married and his wife had gone to work as a labourer along with her husband on the date of the incident.
Thus, a suggestion is given to this witness that when the sister-in- law of the victim was available at home, then why she had not narrated about the incident to her sister-in-law.

This witness admits that there are The State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Vishnu Kushwaha on 2 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118723695/

sentences.text: She also admitted that she had not received any compensation on account of making a such complaint.
8. PW-3 is the Doctor, who had examined the accused.
9. P.W.-4, Shri Devendra Kumar Shrivastava, Assistant Teacher, stated that date of birth of the victim in school record was mentioned as 03.04.1997.
This witness admits that he cannot state as to who had filled the form of the victim and who had brought the victim for admission.
He admits that he had not seen the admission form.
He admits that he has no idea as to which of the documents were furnished in support of date of birth of the victim.
He admits that at Sl. No.375 where name of the victim is mentioned, there are two different handwritings.
He admits that he had not seen any NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:9384 4 CRA-166-2016 document in regard to admission of the victim.
10. Dr. Meena Namdeo (P.W.-6) had examined the victim.
She had found that her hymen was old torn.
There were no injury marks of immediate intercourse.
No opinion could be given in regard to immediate violation of privacy.
She had directed to conduct X-ray for age determination and as per X-ray, age was reported by the Radiologist to be between 17 to 18 years.
She admitted that there can be a difference of age of six months between 17 to 18 years.
11. When these facts are taken into consideration, then firstly prosecution has not proved the date of birth of the victim.

Law in this behalf is laid down in case of Birad Mal Singhvi Vs. Anand Purohit,
AIR 1988 SC 1796, it is held that if the entry in the Scholars Register regarding date of birth is made on the basis of information given by parents, the entry would have evidentiary value but if it is given by a stranger or by someone else who had no special means of knowledge of the date of birth, such an entry will have no evidentiary value.

sentences.text: 12. In the present case, PW-2, mother of the victim, has admitted that she had not taken her daughter for admission to the school.
Victim (PW-1) stated that one of her younger brother was playing in a neighborhood garden.
P.W.- 2 has stated that even he had gone to work as a labourer.

P.W.-4, School Teacher has admitted that there is no mention of this fact as to who had admitted the victim, therefore, in absence of any documentary evidence in regard to date of birth of the victim, in terms of Section 94 of Juvenile Justice Act, when ossification test report is available on record,
which shows that the age of victim was between 17 to 18 years and lady doctor has admitted that there can be variance of about six months, then it is evident that at the time of the incident victim was an adult.
13. Victim has not given any explanation for not raising an alarm.
Though, she admitted that there are several households of her community in immediate neighborhood.
She has also admitted that her younger brother was playing in a nearby garden.
There is no explanation that why victim had not informed her sister-in-law, who admittedly returned back to victim's home on the same day after performing her work as a labourer, about the incident.

The State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Vishnu Kushwaha on 2 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118723695/
3 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:9384 5 CRA-166-2016 Thus, not only delay in FIR under the given facts and circumstances, but also that victim was a adult and her conduct in not raising any alarm and not reporting the matter immediately leaves no iota of doubt that victim being a consenting adult, conviction could not have been sustained by the trial Court and has rightly recorded a finding of acquittal which does not call for any interference, therefore, criminal appeal fails and is dismissed.
